en: The Sūtra on Wrong Views Spoken by the Buddha;
the name of the translator is lost, now appended to the Catalogue of the Eastern Jin.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Venerable Ānanda was in the city of Rājagṛha at the Kalandaka [Nivāpa].
At the Bamboo Grove.

Not long after the Blessed One had attained parinirvāṇa, a certain heterodox practitioner who was a childhood friend of the Venerable Ānanda, wandering about after his midday meal, approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having arrived, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Ānanda.
Having exchanged greetings and offered words of comfort, he sat down to one side.
Once the Ajivika had sat down to one side, he said to the Venerable Ānanda:
"I wish to ask a question; please listen to my question."
“Ask him, worthy one!
Having heard this, Ajita understood it.
“This is Ānanda! he said.
That ascetic Gautama!

Having abandoned wrong views and eliminated wrong views, he does not declare or explain that the world is eternal, nor that the world is non-eternal; that the world is finite, nor that the world is infinite; that the life-principle is the same as the body, nor that the life-principle is different from the body; that there is an end to this life, nor that there is no end to this life; that there both is and is not an end to this life, nor that there neither is nor is not an end to this life.
"Ānanda! Does that ascetic Gautama know wrong view in such a way as it ought to be known?"
“O Brahmin! That Blessed One is wise and possessed of knowledge and vision;

he is the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Having abandoned wrong views and eliminated wrong views, he does not declare that the world is eternal, nor does he declare it to be non-existent at the end of life.”
"O brāhmaṇa! That Blessed One possesses knowledge and vision; he knows that this is a wrong view, and thus the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, should understand it in this way."
"Ānanda! That ascetic Gautama has abandoned wrong views and eliminated wrong views;
he does not declare or teach that the world is eternal, nor does he declare it to be non-existent until the end of life."
"How is it, Ānanda?
Does that śramaṇa Gautama know this wrong view?
How does he know it?"
“O Brahmin! That Blessed One is wise and possessed of vision;

he is the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Having abandoned wrong views and eliminated wrong views, he does not declare that the world is eternal, nor does he declare it to be non-existent at the end of life.”
"O Brahmin! This one with wrong views is associated and thoroughly associated with such a course, such a rebirth, and such a future world. O Brahmin!"
That Blessed One, thus knowing, possessing knowledge and vision, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows wrong view; it should be known in this way.
"Therefore, Ānanda, I now take refuge in you.
"O brāhmaṇa! [he replied.]
"Do not take refuge in me; as I have taken refuge in the Blessed One, you too should take refuge in him.

"Therefore, Ānanda, I now take refuge in that Blessed One, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha of bhikṣus. I am a lay follower (upāsaka) of that Blessed One; from this day forth, I abstain from taking life. Today I take refuge in the Venerable One."
Thus spoke Ānanda.
Having heard what the Venerable Ānanda had said, that Ajīvika was filled with joy and delight.
This concludes the Discourse on Wrong View spoken by the Buddha.
